issues.description: Project IDs are interpolated into URL paths without percent-encoding, allowing path/query manipulation.
Project IDs in batch-create URLs are unescaped and can alter the requested endpoint.
Task IDs are unescaped in annotation-list URLs, enabling path traversal into other routes.
Annotation IDs are unescaped in review URLs and can inject query strings or change route shape.
Transport errors and timeouts are not retried or wrapped, so transient network failures leak raw httpx exceptions.
Retry-After parsing only supports numeric seconds and ignores valid HTTP-date retry headers.
Backoff cap is applied before jitter, so actual sleep can exceed backoff_cap despite the documented cap.
Pagination assumes successful responses contain a valid JSON object with items/next_cursor and does not raise typed errors for malformed bodies.
Batch-create assumes a results field exists and lets KeyError/JSON parsing errors escape on malformed successful responses.
Batch-create does not validate that returned batch indexes are complete, unique, and within the submitted chunk.
BatchItemResult.from_dict accepts invalid statuses and inconsistent task/error combinations.
ReviewResult.from_dict accepts invalid verdict values despite the public Literal type.
Project parsing exposes raw KeyError/TypeError/ValueError instead of contextual client-side schema errors.
Frozen dataclasses contain mutable dict fields, so model instances are not actually immutable.
Scripted mock responses bypass API-key validation, which can hide auth behavior mistakes in tests.
Development tooling only includes pytest; there is no configured linting, typing, coverage, or packaging check.
Package version is duplicated manually instead of deriving from project metadata, inviting release drift.
